chunks: But none of them put faith in Moses except some youths among his people who were nonetheless afraid lest the Pharaoh and his nobles should persecute them; for the Pharaoh was mighty in the land, and guilty of excesses.

key_terms.الْمُسْرِفِينَ: the transgressors / those who exceed bounds

ai.seo_question: Who believed in Moses among his people and why were they afraid?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the term 'dhurriyyah' (offspring/descendants) is often interpreted to refer specifically to the youth or the elite of the Israelites who maintained faith amidst the tyranny of Pharaoh. This verse underscores the theme of 'khawf' (fear) as a protective mechanism for believers during periods of oppression, a concept central to Shia understanding of the Ahl al-Bayt's endurance. It highlights the contrast between the transgressive power of the oppressor and the cautious piety of the faithful remnant.
